deals.notes: Harrodsburg Marketplace is a 60,048 SF Kroger-anchored neighborhood center on S. College Street (US-127) in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, roughly 30 miles southwest of Lexington, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. The story is the anchor: Kroger has operated here since October 1987, occupies 60% of the GLA at $7.05/SF, does $858 PSF of 2025 sales (about $31.0 million, up 13% since 2022) at a 1.10% health ratio, exercised its most recent option in 2023 without landlord concessions, and holds three more five-year options that would carry the term to roughly 2043. That is as strong a grocery credit position as this portfolio offers, and it produces 52% of the center's revenue. In-place CY2027 NOI is $455,218 on $654,519 of effective gross revenue against $199,301 of operating expenses, at an $8.88/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $10.60/SF modeled market rent. Below the anchor the picture is thinner. WALT is only 2.07 years on current terms, 79% of GLA is scheduled to roll in 2028, and the near-term roll starts almost immediately: Feeders Pet Supply, a gross lease with no expense recovery on 9% of the GLA, expires in February 2027, and Smoke World's roster term is a modeled option exercise that the OM itself says ownership expects the tenant may miss. Arby's, at 16% of base rent on a 3.8%-of-GLA pad, expires June 2028 already at market rent. The value-add case is the single 3,600 SF vacancy plus genuine mark-to-market on Wah Mei Chinese at $8.14/SF and Cricket Wireless at $10.75/SF against a $14.00/SF UPS Store lease signed in April 2026 — the best available read on real shop market rent here. The constraint is the trade area: 10,510 people within three miles, $68,376 average household income and the slowest income growth in this group, which limits how far shop rents can be pushed and argues for cap-rate cushion behind an otherwise excellent grocery box.

59% OF THE GLA RECOVERS LITTLE OR NOTHING. Missy's Beauty (9,100 SF) recovers $0 and Food Lion (30,280 SF) recovers only $1.03/SF against the center's $2.50-$3.00/SF shop rate. The center recovers $101,714 against $178,468 of operating expenses — a 57% recovery ratio. Every dollar of expense growth on those two suites, including the next Robeson County revaluation, falls to ownership.

China Garden carries a 16.59% occupancy cost on $138 PSF of sales (OM-stated) at the center's second-highest rent, $19.84/SF. That ratio is roughly double a sustainable restaurant level. The lease runs to December 2030 but this is the row most likely to go dark.

Jackson Hewitt pays $25.20/SF — the highest rent at the center, roughly 3x the center average — for a SEASONAL tax-preparation use with no disclosed sales. That is above-market rent that may not survive the December 2029 renewal, and it inflates the in-place NOI a buyer would capitalize. Do not read it as a market comp.

The OM's own page-3 sales figure for Food Lion (~$11.3M) does not reconcile with the rent roll's $393 PSF and 1.57% health ratio, both of which imply ~$11.9M. A 5% discrepancy on the anchor's sales in a four-bullet highlights page is worth running down.

Sales are disclosed for only three of eleven tenants (Food Lion, Dollar Tree, China Garden), and one of the three is the center's problem tenant. Nothing is known about Missy's Beauty, Pawn Plus, Rent-A-Center or Jackson Hewitt — 21,900 SF and 35% of base rent between them.
Two of eleven suites are tobacco/vape or pawn uses (Express Discount Tobacco, Pawn Plus) — categories that carry regulatory sensitivity and can complicate financing and future re-tenanting.
Taxes are NOT reassessed in the pro-forma, and with 59% of the GLA on capped or gross recovery structures, a revaluation flows disproportionately to ownership.

deals.notes: Lumber River is a 66,781 SF Food Lion-anchored neighborhood center immediately off Interstate 95 (59,500 AADT) on W 5th Street in Lumberton, North Carolina, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 100% leased — the only fully-occupied asset in this group other than Fort Howard Square — and produces $463,149 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $641,617 of effective gross revenue against $178,468 of operating expenses, at an $8.08/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $10.32/SF modeled market rent. Food Lion has anchored the center since August 1985, occupies 45.3% of the GLA at $5.13/SF, and runs an excellent store at roughly $11.9 million of sales, $393 PSF, and a 1.57% occupancy cost; the co-tenancy is genuinely national for a market this size, with Dollar Tree, Rent-A-Center, Pizza Hut and Subway. The value-add case is the 24,900 SF rolling between 2029 and 2031 plus two deeply below-market suites — Missy's Beauty at $4.22/SF gross on 9,100 SF and Dollar Tree at $6.74/SF against a 5.62% occupancy cost. Two things cut against it. First, the trade area is contracting: 3-mile population has fallen 23% since 2010, to 12,227, with a $49,095 median household income and a further decline projected — mark-to-market spreads mean less where the customer base is shrinking, and this deserves genuine cap-rate cushion. Second, 59% of the GLA recovers little or nothing, because Missy's Beauty pays gross and Food Lion recovers only $1.03/SF, leaving a 57% expense-recovery ratio and putting the next Robeson County revaluation squarely on ownership. Watch China Garden, which carries a 16.59% occupancy cost at the center's second-highest rent, and Jackson Hewitt, whose $25.20/SF on a seasonal use is above-market rent inflating the in-place NOI rather than a comp to build on.

TWO OF THE THREE HIGHEST RENTS LOOK ABOVE MARKET WITH NO SALES TO SUPPORT THEM. Mills Veterinary Care pays $28.18/SF against CBRE's own $22.00/SF assumption for that size — 28% above — and T-Mobile pays $24.97/SF against the same $22.00/SF, with T-Mobile EXPIRING OCTOBER 2027 in year one with no disclosed option. Above-market rent on a near-term expiry resets down; treat the $53,924 as at risk rather than as durable income.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT AT THE CENTER. Not one of the seventeen occupied suites has productivity data — including Ollie's, Dollar Tree and the two above-market shop rents. Tenant health simply cannot be assessed from this book.

Near-term rollover is front-loaded and unprotected: Hair Cuttery (July 2027), T-Mobile (October 2027), Rent-A-Center (March 2028), Anytime Fitness (February 2028) and H&R Block (April 2028) — 13,560 SF and roughly $236,000 of base rent — all expire within about sixteen months of the analysis start with no disclosed options, and CBRE's in-place NOI assumes they simply hold over at current rents.

The roster is heavily franchised and local-operator: Anytime Fitness, H&R Block, Wireless Zone, Wright Fight Concepts, D&F Foods and possibly McDonald's and T-Mobile are all likely franchisee or dealer entities rather than corporate credit, and no guaranties are disclosed. The OM's '44.5% of revenue from national credit tenants' claim should be tested lease by lease.

McDonald's ground lease is presented as parcelizable optionality, but no ROFR, ROFO or purchase option is disclosed. McDonald's pad leases commonly carry one, and it would block a spin-off. Read the lease before crediting that value.

upsideItems.item: Lease up the single 8,000 SF vacancy
upsideItems.detail: Lease up the single 8,000 SF vacancy (10.1% of GLA). CBRE models it absorbed 1/1/2028 at $15.00/SF on a 10-year NNN term, taking NOI from $773,224 to $919,324 — nearly the whole of the modeled CY2028 step. Budget the ~$320,000 of tenant improvements and $113,360 of commissions, and stress-test the $15.00/SF against P.Y. Kitchen's actual October 2026 signing at $13.00/SF.

upsideItems.item: 30.3% of GLA rolls inside the hold
upsideItems.detail: 24,003 SF (30.3% of GLA) expires during the hold, which is the OM's stated mark-to-market window. In-place rent is $12.85/SF against CBRE's $14.37/SF 2027 weighted-average market rent, and the modeled cash flow reaches $1,128,437 of NOI by CY2036 — 45.9% growth over the in-place figure.

upsideItems.item: Ollie's options run to a potential 2045
upsideItems.detail: Ollie's holds three additional five-year options to a potential 2045, which is exceptional term security on 31.5% of the GLA from a growing national discount retailer. The $8.00/SF rent is actually above CBRE's $6.00/SF junior-anchor market assumption, so this is fairly-priced, durable income rather than upside — its value is that it makes the rest of the business plan financeable.

upsideItems.item: Parcelize and spin off the McDonald's ground lease
upsideItems.detail: The McDonald's ground lease is a genuine structuring lever: $80,525 of ground rent on a separately identifiable pad, in place since 2000, running to October 2031, with CBRE modeling a $30.00/SF pad market rent against $23.01/SF in place. A parcelized McDonald's ground lease trades far tighter than an 89.9%-leased Burlington County strip — subject to confirming there is no ROFR.

upsideItems.item: $107,839 3-mile average household income
upsideItems.detail: Genuinely strong trade-area income for a small community: $107,839 average household income within three miles ($84,403 median) and $111,966 across the true trade area. Combined with a constrained, semi-rural supply picture, that supports the shop rents better than the population count alone suggests.

upsideItems.item: Deborah Heart & Lung and Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst
upsideItems.detail: Two large, stable employment anchors: the Deborah Heart and Lung Center with 1,370 employees is CONTIGUOUS to the property, and Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst with 42,000+ active-duty, civilian and family members sits six miles north — daytime demand that is largely recession- and e-commerce-insensitive.

upsideItems.item: New Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell in the node
upsideItems.detail: The retail node is visibly improving: the obsolete former Browns Mills Shopping Center down Broadway Street was demolished in May 2026 to make way for a Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell — new national investment that validates the node and adds traffic without adding directly competing shop space.

upsideItems.item: Two large suites are locked well below market
upsideItems.detail: Happy Taps Spirits at $10.00/SF and Community Dental at $8.00/SF sit far below CBRE's $16.50/SF assumption for space that size. Both recover $6.37/SF on top and both run to 2034-2035, so the spread is secure income rather than capturable upside — but it means the in-place rent roll is not carrying hidden downside on those 9,840 SF.

deals.notes: Pine Grove Plaza is a 79,306 SF neighborhood center at Broadway Street and Trenton Road in Browns Mills, Pemberton Township, New Jersey, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 89.9% leased and produces $773,224 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $1,191,176 of effective gross revenue against $417,951 of operating expenses, at a $12.85/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $14.37/SF modeled market rent. The owned anchor is a 24,963 SF Ollie's Bargain Outlet at $8.00/SF with a current term to October 2030 and three five-year options to a potential 2045; Dollar Tree, Rent-A-Center, McDonald's on a ground lease, Anytime Fitness and H&R Block round out a genuinely daily-needs roster. The traffic thesis, however, rests on a 38,000 SF ACME Markets that is NOT part of the offering — it occupies a contiguous building ownership does not control, is the only ACME within ten miles and the busiest of sixteen grocers in the trade area, and comes with no lease, no term and no go-dark protection whatsoever. Two other items shape the underwriting. Ollie's contributes zero expense reimbursement on 31.5% of the GLA, leaving a 65% recovery ratio against a New Jersey tax line of $191,133 — $2.41/SF and 25% of NOI — that CBRE expressly did not reassess. And the market rents behind the growth case look optimistic against the center's own recent deals: CBRE assumes $22.00/SF for mid-size shop space, but P.Y. Kitchen signed in October 2026, three months before the projection begins, at $13.00/SF on a nine-year term. The value-add case is the single 8,000 SF vacancy plus 24,003 SF rolling during the hold, and the parcelizable McDonald's ground lease is real optionality if no right of first refusal blocks it. The trade area supports the plan better than its size suggests — $107,839 average household income within three miles, the 1,370-employee Deborah Heart and Lung Center contiguous to the property, Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst six miles north, and a new Tractor Supply, Wawa and Taco Bell replacing the demolished center down the street.

Its economics run through the recovery line ($387,972, 69% of its total revenue) rather than base rent, which is why the center's $14.70/SF weighted-average base rent understates the income intensity of the asset. There is no building mark-to-market on a ground lease; the five undisclosed option rents are what govern income after November 2030.

THE STARBUCKS AND COLD STONE PAD IS SEPARATELY PARCELED, which is why those two tenants carry recoveries of $38.84/SF and $33.98/SF — four to five times the center's $8.00-$8.82/SF shop rate. TWO LEASES COMMENCE ON 1 JANUARY 2027 — Bar Forno ($103,034) and Kleen Kar Car Wash ($48,000) — the first day of the analysis period. NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $2,272,874 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED, AND THIS IS NEW JERSEY WITH THE HEAVIEST TAX LOAD IN THIS PORTFOLIO GROUP. The $767,111 CY2027 real-estate tax line is $4.88/SF — 64% of total operating expenses and 34% of NOI — and the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. New Jersey municipalities revalue on their own schedules and a sale commonly draws the assessor's attention; confirm Washington Township's revaluation status and the property's assessment-to-true-value ratio before bidding. The mitigant is that recoveries are strong here (98% of operating expenses), so most of an increase would pass through — but not on ACME's NNN+5% structure or on the tenants with below-rate recoveries.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT, and ACME's are expressly described as ANECDOTAL ($24.7 million, $374 PSF). The ±556,000 and ±469,400 customer-visit figures are Placer.ai traffic counts, not sales.

The current term ends September 2029 and a single five-year option would carry it to roughly 2034 — after which a 20,742 SF box with heavy gym build-out has no contractual protection at all. NEW JERSEY TAXES ARE $767,111 — $4.88/SF, 64% of operating expenses and 34% of NOI — and are expressly NOT reassessed. This is the heaviest tax load in the portfolio group by a wide margin. A Washington Township revaluation or a post-sale assessment increase is the single largest quantifiable risk to the NOI, partially mitigated by strong recoveries but not on ACME's lighter NNN+5% structure.

$151,034 OF CY2027 BASE RENT (6.6%) COMES FROM TWO LEASES THAT COMMENCE ON THE FIRST DAY OF THE ANALYSIS PERIOD — Bar Forno ($103,034) and the Kleen Kar Car Wash ground lease ($48,000), both dated 1 January 2027. None of it is in-place income today. Confirm delivery, opening and rent commencement, and ask what free rent or landlord work sits behind those rates.

CHEF CHUN PAYS $35.84/SF, 43% ABOVE CBRE'S OWN $25.00/SF MARKET ASSUMPTION, with no sales disclosed, and expires March 2028. Above-market rent on a near-term expiry inflates the NOI a buyer capitalizes and can reset DOWN at renewal. The same pattern, more mildly, applies to H&R Block at $29.38/SF on a seasonal use.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT, and the anchor's are ANECDOTAL by the OM's own word ($24.7 million, $374 PSF). The impressive ±556,000 and ±469,400 figures are foot-traffic counts, not sales. Tenant health across a 157,300 SF center cannot be assessed from this book.

MBM Sports' 2,700 SF suite 005A pays $1.48/SF with zero recovery. If that space is storage or mezzanine rather than leasable retail, it is inflating the 157,300 SF GLA — which in turn flatters the 99.4% occupancy figure and understates any price-per-square-foot. Verify the measurement.

Leslie's Pool Supplies (3,440 SF) is a public company under real financial strain that has been closing stores; Rudi's Formal Wear is in a structurally declining category; and Today's Cleaners brings dry-cleaning environmental diligence. None is large, but all three warrant specific attention.

The 27,031 SF of pad sites the OM flags for 'parcelization and spin-off' is presented as clean optionality, but NO purchase option, right of first refusal or right of first offer is disclosed for Bank of America, McDonald's-style ground tenants or any pad. Ground leases on bank and QSR pads frequently carry an ROFR that would block a sale. Read the leases before crediting that value.

The Starbucks/Cold Stone 3,050 SF pad is ALREADY separately parceled, which proves the mechanics work here. Confirm no ROFRs block a sale.

upsideItems.item: $137,604 3-mile average household income
upsideItems.detail: An exceptionally strong trade area: 149,910 people and 54,866 households with a $130,247 average household income, and within three miles $137,604 average and $116,957 median household income — the highest in this entire portfolio group. High income AND high density together justify the above-average rents, support a tighter going-in cap, and mark this as a supply-constrained infill location rather than a suburban strip.

upsideItems.item: 21.8-year average tenure, 63.2% e-commerce resistant
upsideItems.detail: Remarkable tenure and stability: a 21.8-year average operating tenure, with nearly 55% of the GLA in occupancy for over 25 years and 70% for more than 15 — and 63.2% of revenue from e-commerce-resistant tenants (dining, fitness, grocery, services, automotive).

upsideItems.item: 99.4% leased with no lease-up risk
upsideItems.detail: Functionally full at 99.4% leased with a single 984 SF vacancy — no lease-up risk, no vacancy carry, and no speculative absorption assumption underpinning the projections.

upsideItems.item: Rowan University and the Route 42 corridor
upsideItems.detail: Rowan University (±24,500 enrolled) sits within the 5-mile ring alongside Gloucester Premium Outlets, and the center's position between NJ Route 42 and Hurffville-Cross Keys Road captures both daily commuters and seasonal shore traffic.

deals.notes: Washington Center Shoppes is a 157,300 SF grocery-anchored community center on 28.9 acres at Egg Harbor Road and Greentree Road in Sewell, New Jersey, between Route 42 and Hurffville-Cross Keys Road in the Philadelphia MSA, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is the largest and highest-quality asset in this group: 99.4% leased with a single 984 SF vacancy, $2,272,874 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $3,464,543 of effective gross revenue, a 21.8-year average tenant tenure with 55% of the GLA in place more than 25 years, and the strongest demographics in the portfolio at $137,604 average household income within three miles and $130,247 across a 149,910-person trade area. ACME Markets anchors 42% of the GLA on a GROUND LEASE at $2.59/SF — the tenant owns its building, so its economics run through $387,972 of recoveries rather than rent — with anecdotal sales of $24.7 million, ±556,000 annual visits and five remaining five-year options to a potential 2055. Planet Fitness, the busiest of six within ten miles and top 20% nationally by chain, holds 20,742 SF to September 2029 with one option left. The tenancy underneath is genuinely good — Chipotle, Starbucks, First Watch, Bank of America on a ground lease at $200,000, Jersey Mike's, Mavis, Sherwin-Williams — and 63.2% of revenue comes from e-commerce-resistant uses. The clearest lever is the 27,031 SF of pad sites with dedicated parking that the OM flags for parcelization and spin-off into the single-tenant net-lease market, a mechanic already proven here by the separately-parceled Starbucks/Cold Stone pad. Three things need work before pricing. Eighty percent of the GLA is rolled by the end of 2030, including ACME and Planet Fitness, and the OM prints none of their option rents. The New Jersey tax line is $767,111 — $4.88/SF, 34% of NOI — and is expressly not reassessed. And the first-year expiries cluster in the most stretched suites, with Starbucks at a $97.19/SF all-in cost and Cold Stone at $70.83/SF both rolling in 2027 off the same separately-parceled pad, while $151,034 of 2027 base rent comes from two leases that commence on the very first day of the projection.

THE $8,400 PLANET AID PARKING LICENCE is real income but is NOT rent: it is a donation-bin licence, modeled flat with zero growth across all eleven projection years. It is inside the $702,350 EGR and therefore inside the $492,981 NOI. At 1.7% of NOI it is not material to value, but confirm its term and cancellability rather than capitalizing it like a lease.

GROCERY OUTLET'S LEASE IS BRAND NEW AND SHORT: commenced 1 November 2025, primary term to 31 October 2030 — five years on a grocery anchor that is 45% of base rent. The OM does not disclose the option structure, which is what actually governs income beyond 2030. This is the single most important missing document in the deal.

GROCERY OUTLET OPERATES THROUGH INDEPENDENT LOCAL OWNER-OPERATORS who control each store's inventory, hiring and marketing (the OM says so on page 2). Confirm whether the lease is with Grocery Outlet Holding Corp. or with the local operator entity, and whether a corporate guaranty exists — the credit answer differs enormously between the two.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $492,981 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED, AND THIS IS PENNSYLVANIA — the state where our tax-reassessment work has found the most value and the most risk. The $61,006 CY2027 tax line is the 2026 budget grown 3% annually; the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. Cumberland County uses a stale base-year assessment adjusted by an annually-republished Common Level Ratio, so the exposure here is NOT an automatic sale-price reset but an assessment appeal or CLR movement. Verify the current-year Cumberland County CLR (republished each July) and the property's base-year assessment before bidding. At $1.21/SF the modeled tax line is low for a Pennsylvania retail center and is 12% of NOI.

CBRE MODELS A 16-MONTH ABSORPTION WINDOW for the 9,970 SF of vacancy (1/1/2027 to 5/1/2028) — longer than the 12 months used elsewhere in this portfolio, which is an honest acknowledgment that 8,780 SF of it is junior-box rather than small-shop space.

TWO 2026 LEASES AND A 2024 LEASE UNDERCUT CBRE'S SMALL-SHOP MARKET RENT. Ella Rose Massage signed in April 2026 at $17.50/SF and Divine Thread signed in April 2024 at $16.00/SF, both below the $20.00/SF CBRE assumes for sub-2,000 SF space; Sophia's Pizzeria signed in November 2024 at $16.36/SF against a $16.50/SF assumption for 2,000-5,000 SF space, which does validate the mid-size assumption. Weigh the actual signings, not just the assumption sheet, when underwriting the lease-up.

The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, renewal-option terms, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated. No footer date stamp appears on the Fairview pro-forma pages, so omDate is left null (the sister Project Evergreen books are stamped July-August 2026).

upsideItems.item: Lease up 9,970 SF (19.7% of GLA)
upsideItems.detail: Lease up 9,970 SF across three suites (19.7% of GLA) — the dominant driver of CBRE's 85.5% ten-year NOI growth and 6.53% CAGR. NOI is modeled to jump from $488,776 in CY2027 to $680,675 in CY2028 on that absorption alone. Budget the $359,419 of CY2028 TI and $55,341 of commissions against it, and note CBRE allowed 16 months rather than 12 because 8,780 SF of it is junior-box space.

upsideItems.item: Grocery Outlet does $853 PSF at a 2.16% occupancy cost
upsideItems.detail: Grocery Outlet is an outstanding store: $14.2 million of sales, $853 PSF, at a computed 2.16% occupancy cost — among the strongest grocery productivity in this entire portfolio group — in a trade area served by only two grocers. That performance is what makes the 2030 option decision very likely to go the landlord's way, once the option terms are known.

upsideItems.detail: Jackson Hewitt at $10.48/SF against a $20.00/SF market rent for space that size is the deepest single shop mark-to-market in the deal, and it expires May 2030 — inside a normal hold. LHM Physical Therapy at $15.12/SF against $16.50/SF adds a smaller increment in June 2029.

upsideItems.item: Dollar Tree is deeply below market but locked to 2033
upsideItems.detail: Dollar Tree at $6.00/SF against CBRE's $9.00/SF assumption for that suite is 50% below market on 21.4% of the GLA. It is secure, very sticky income from an investment-grade credit in place 25 years — but the December 2033 expiry sits beyond a normal 5-7 year hold, so treat it as durability rather than capturable upside.

upsideItems.item: High-barrier, high-income Harrisburg-adjacent trade area
upsideItems.detail: A genuinely strong and high-barrier trade area for a center this size: 63,350 people within three miles at a $91,662 average household income, and a true trade area of 44,800 people at $117,595 average income and $98,189 median. New Cumberland is a dense, historic, built-out suburb directly across the Susquehanna from the state capital — supply is constrained, which supports both rents and a tighter going-in cap than the headline NOI alone suggests.

upsideItems.item: Between I-83 and the PA Turnpike
upsideItems.detail: Superior commuter and logistics positioning between I-83 (36,700 AADT) and the Pennsylvania Turnpike (42,500 AADT), across the river from Harrisburg and within reach of York, Carlisle, Mechanicsburg and Hershey — a daytime population of 81,457 within three miles against a resident population of 63,350.

upsideItems.detail: Dairy Queen holds a drive-thru position through August 2032 — the most valuable and least replaceable small-shop configuration at the center.

deals.notes: Fairview Commons is a 50,485 SF Grocery Outlet-anchored neighborhood center on Old York Road in New Cumberland, Pennsylvania — a dense, built-out, high-barrier suburb directly across the Susquehanna River from Harrisburg — offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is 80.3% leased and produces $492,981 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $702,350 of effective gross revenue against $209,369 of operating expenses, at a $12.83/SF weighted-average base rent versus CBRE's $14.84/SF modeled market rent. Grocery Outlet is the reason to look: 16,650 SF doing $14.2 million of sales at $853 PSF and a computed 2.16% occupancy cost, one of only two grocers serving the trade area, and among the strongest grocery productivity in this portfolio. But its lease commenced only in November 2025 with a five-year primary term to October 2030 and the OM never prints the option structure — on 45% of the base rent, that is the first document to get. The value-add case is the 9,970 SF of vacancy, and CBRE's own 16-month absorption window is an honest signal that 8,780 SF of it is junior-box rather than small-shop space; the modeled jump from $488,776 to $680,675 of NOI between 2027 and 2028 carries $415,000 of tenant improvements and commissions behind it. The trade area supports the plan: 63,350 people within three miles at $91,662 average household income, a true trade area averaging $117,595, and a three-mile daytime population of 81,457 against 63,350 residents. Two cautions on the income itself. Smoker's Express pays $26.18/SF, 31% above CBRE's own market rent for space that size, with no sales disclosed — above-market rent that inflates the capitalized NOI and can reset down at its 2029 expiry — while three leases actually signed between 2024 and 2026 came in at $16.00 to $17.50/SF. And this is Pennsylvania, where the modeled $1.21/SF tax line is expressly unreassessed and the real exposure runs through Cumberland County's base-year assessment and its annually-republished Common Level Ratio rather than a sale-triggered reset.
